title: Console beta probe interview summaries and backlog groom
highlights: Participants expect cost/latency tradeoffs surfaced at point of model selection, not buried in per-route settings.
Rollout UI (canary %) confused: users attempted to type percent values then gave up and used tickets instead.
Preview/simulate panel idea resonated — customers want a quick estimate of cost and p95 latency for a specific request pattern.
Inline help and short examples reduce friction more than adding another settings page.
Several platform engineers asked for a ‘dry-run’ mode for routing + fallback to validate traffic split behavior.
content:
Study: unmoderated + moderated probe interviews during beta deployment (Feb 3–9 2026). Goal: identify where console UX breaks down when teams try to onboard a new model, create per-route rollouts, and reason about cost/latency impact.

Participants: 7 customers (mix of platform engineers and ML engineers). Sample: fintech-platform (1), health-tech (2), mid-market SaaS (2), consumer app (2). Sessions: 45–60m; recorded and lightly transcribed.

Protocol summary: quick task scenarios (create route, pin model variant, schedule a 10% canary rollout, estimate cost impact for 100k tokens/month). After tasks: semi-structured debrief and ask for feature wishlist.

Verbatim quotes (selected):
- "I don't want to be a billing person while debugging models — show me the tradeoff up front." — platform engineer, fintech
- "Where do I change the fallback model? I clicked everywhere." — ML engineer, health-tech
- "The slider is cute but I tried to type 5 and it insisted on 500.\nFeels brittle." — infra lead, consumer app
- "A preview that runs a sample input and shows latency + tokens would be gold." — product engineer, SaaS

Key findings and implications: 
1) Model selection affordance: users expect immediate per-model metadata (p95, per-token cost, recommended quantization flag). Many scanned the model list for a quick signal and resorted to external docs when the list lacked inline numbers.
   Implication: add small metrics row under each model in the picker (p95-preview, cost estimate for baseline 1k tokens, tags like "low-latency").

2) Rollout UX friction: the current canary modal is multi-step and hides the actual percent control behind an advanced menu. Participants tried typing values, then used the slider. The slider's sensitivity made small percentages hard to hit.
   Implication: replace slider-only control with combined numeric input + slider; persist last-used value per-project. Add quick presets (1%, 5%, 10%).

3) Cost & latency preview: almost all participants wanted a sandboxed estimate feature — give them a simulation that uses sample token lengths and distribution to show estimated monthly cost and p95. They treated the estimate as a guardrail for choosing model variants.
   Implication: add a lightweight "simulate" panel on route configuration that accepts sample payload size and traffic assumptions.

4) Visibility into fallback and routing policies: users couldn't find which fallback would be used if a model failed. The concept of fallback as "policy priority list" wasn't represented visually.
   Implication: surface a small ordered list of fallback candidates with explicit labels (primary, fallback-1, fallback-2) and a test button to simulate a failure.

5) Inline help beats docs: when stuck, people want 1–2 line microcopy and an example rather than a link out to Confluence.
   Implication: add microcopy and an example toggle next to non-obvious controls (quantization, KV cache TTL, route timeout).

Wireframe writeups (low-fi — sketches described for engineering handoff):
- Wireframe A: Model + Route two-column matrix. Left column: compact model list with 3-line metadata (model name, p95-preview, est cost/1k). Center: search + filter by latency/cost/size. Right column (route editor): top row route name and enable SWITCH, row below rollout control with numeric input + slider + presets, below that simulate panel with sample input size and traffic slider and output of est cost + est p95 and token breakdown. Footer: save + dry-run.
- Wireframe B: Inline route accordion. Each route row in the routes table expands to show rollout controls, fallback list, and a small simulate card. The advantage is less context switching and faster scanning for teams managing many routes.

Backlog grooming (prioritized during session):
- UX-889: Add numeric input + slider for canary percent + presets (1,5,10) — priority: P0, estimate: 3 (owner: Ravi).
- INF-2341: Simulate panel MVP (sample tokens, traffic, estimated cost + p95) — priority: P0, estimate: 8 (owner: Marin).
- INF-2410: Inline model metadata in picker (p95, est cost/1k, tag badges) — priority: P1, estimate: 5 (owner: Olga).
- UX-900: Fallback policy visualizer + test button — priority: P1, estimate: 5 (owner: Derek).
- INF-2455: Microcopy + example snippets for quantization and KV cache fields — priority: P2, estimate: 2 (owner: Content/Docs).

Notes on scope: simulate panel MVP should not run live tokens at first — it's a heuristic estimate using historical model traces and weighted token length presets. Later iterations can add sampling against a customer-owned dataset (opt-in).

Open questions surfaced during interviews: 
- Do we show dollar estimates by default or behind an "estimate" toggle to avoid alarming non-payment-users?
- What privacy constraints apply if we offer a sample-run that sends a sample payload to a model variant (customer concerns about PII)?
- Should dry-run simulate routing logic across dedicated and hosted pools or only within the chosen deployment type?

Immediate next steps / action items: 
- (This week) Create low-fi prototype for Wireframe A (Ravi + Olga) to test internally with SRE and one beta customer (target: Feb 22).
- (2 weeks) Implement canary control change as small frontend PR (UX-889) and ship behind a feature flag (owner: Ravi, target: Mar 3).
- (1 month) Kick off INF-2341 design spike: backend feasibility for simulate panel and data sources for latency/cost estimates (owner: Marin, target: Mar 10).
- Add microcopy for quantization field in console (owner: Docs, target: Feb 19).

Appendix: session-level rough notes (short):
- Customer A (fintech): worried about showing dollar amounts, wants per-environment toggles (prod/non-prod).
- Customer B (health): strong desire for dry-run + audit log entry whenever rollouts change.
- Customer C (SaaS): likes table accordion approach for many routes.

Risks called out: inaccurate simulation could mislead teams into choosing suboptimal models; slider-only rollout control leads to misconfigurations; exposing raw dollar numbers without context could cause support volume spikes.

Overall recommendation: prioritize canary control improvement + simulate panel MVP + inline model metadata. These three changes address the majority of blockers observed in sessions and keep the scope manageable for an initial beta polish.

Contact: Marin Alvarez (marin@redwood.ai) for follow-ups.
